place.en: Bhairab Jute Mill · Gate 1 · Thursday, 11:50 PM

brief.en: Bipin Rai has signed the night gate register every working night for eleven years. He has not been home since the fourteenth — and his signature is still in the register every night since. His wife has a general diary entry at Golabari and no FIR. The mill says he is on duty. The mill is not saying where.

iraNote.en: “Nobody vanishes out of a register. They get written over. Look at the ink before you look for the man.”

teaser.en: A night watchman stopped coming home, and his signature did not stop arriving.

text.en: Bipin Rai signed every night. From the 15th the ink is black — his own pen is blue — and the loops close the other way.
B. Rai, night duty, Shalimar godown, effective the 15th. Typed. Office stamp in the corner. No signature anywhere on it.
Bipin Rai, drawn in full, at Bhairab. The Shalimar sheet carries no watchman’s post at all.
Trunk, blanket, a tin of mustard oil, all where he left them. The cycle and the flask are gone.
Seven nights chalked on the wall in fives, and one name written small in the corner: B. Rai.
Lodged the 19th by Parul Rai. No FIR taken — noted “the man is on duty elsewhere, per the mill”.
A country liquor bottle in the nettles. Nothing worth lifting off it.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — by the moss on it, it has been there since the monsoon

label.en: CHIT FUND RECEIPT · IN HIS NAME

text.en: Three instalments behind, the last one paid in March.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — half this night shift is three instalments behind on something

text.en: Dated the 15th. Found folded in the hut with four others like it.

dismissNote.en: ruled out — no hour printed, and he crossed for the market every week of his life

text.en: “Chit 62 came down typed, with a stamp and no name. I put him on the Shalimar cycle and signed the nights myself so the register would not carry a hole.”

hook.en: the register sleeps in his room

confession.en: Signed Bipin Rai’s name into the night register seven times so the gate would not show a hole — and never once asked who typed the chit that made it.

hook.en: drew his full wages on the eighteenth

alibi.en: She drew the pay because the office handed it to her, and she has been at Golabari every third day since asking where the man is. Nobody looking for a husband files a diary entry against herself.

hook.en: types what the offices send down

alibi.en: The gate office machine has a broken lower case ‘e’ and chit 62 has none. He types on the wrong typewriter to have typed this.

hook.en: the stamp on the chit is his office’s

alibi.en: A manager who wanted a watchman gone would post him gone and sign it. This chit is stamped and unsigned — the work of somebody who can reach his drawer but not use his name.

setting.en: The lane behind the mill quarters, a folded diary receipt in her hand.

ask.en: When did he last come home?

answer.en: “The night of the fourteenth. He took the cycle and the flask, the way he takes them every night.”

note.en: Cycle and flask. A man running takes more than that; a man going on duty takes exactly that.

ask.en: You drew his wages on the eighteenth.

answer.en: “The office put them in my hand. Should I have refused, to prove I was worried?”

note.en: Fair. And a mill paying full wages for a man nobody has seen in four days is the half worth pulling.

ask.en: Golabari would not take an FIR.

answer.en: “They wrote it in the diary and told me the mill says he is on duty at Shalimar. So I asked the mill. The mill says he is here.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the general diary entry. She is done being told what she already reported.

note.en: Two answers from the same company, and they cannot both be true.

setting.en: The head durwan’s room by Gate 1, seven brass tokens on a nail.

ask.en: Whose hand is in the register after the fifteenth?

note.en: Not a second’s pause. Either an honest man or one who has had a week to settle the sentence.

answer.en: “It came down typed, with the stamp and no name. I put him on the Shalimar cycle and I signed his nights so the register would not carry a hole.”

lockedHint.en: Pin the transfer chit. He answers paper, and only paper.

note.en: A forged week of signatures to close a hole a typed chit tore open — and he never asked who typed it.

answer.en: “The purchase office and the manager’s office share it. The manager’s room is locked at seven.”

note.en: A stamp sits in a drawer. A signature sits on a man. Somebody chose the drawer.

correction.en: A bottle in the nettles is not a reason. A hole in the night register stops the fortnight’s pay for every man on the gate — that is what he was covering.
Two inks in one column. Only the man the register sleeps beside can write another man’s name into it seven nights running.
Nobody hides a man behind a ferry ticket. A typed chit with a stamp and no name moved Bipin Rai out of this mill on paper — and the head durwan let it stand.

text.en: Two inks say somebody signed for him. The chit says where he was sent. Go and read the wall of the place it sent him to.

bankedClue.en: The night register in two inks — and a transfer chit typed on the office machine, stamped and unsigned
